output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (is/is not by stage and loan type), then competing-hypotheses weighing, with a source check on the dashboard's withdrawal figures
output.brief: The slowdown comes from one clause in the May credit policy refresh, not from Corvane or the new hires. From 1 May, property-secured loans between $150k and $500k need a full inspection appraisal instead of a desktop valuation. The valuation stage for these loans went from about 1.6 days to 8.4 days. The valuation firm's turnaround hasn't changed: about 8.6 days for full appraisals and 1.2 for desktop ones. Full appraisals rose from about 30 a month to about 80. Unsecured loans are back to normal at 5.9 days. Consumer loans on Corvane are flat. Document collection at the new hires' branches matches the other branches. The policy unit never assessed the effect on processing times. Withholding Corvane's payment or putting the new hires on improvement plans would punish the wrong parties. I'm confident in this, about 90%. I haven't established whether the longer waits are what drive withdrawals. Part of the rise is an artifact, because Corvane now auto-closes files after 30 days of inactivity and counts them as withdrawn. Next steps: take the measured delay and the audit rationale (desktop valuations ran 12% high) to the credit risk committee. Add a by-stage view to the dashboard. Check withdrawals separately.
